Subject: EdgeFin: Priority — latency & error surge impacting transactions

Hi Neha / Marissa,

We started seeing a sudden increase in API latency around 07:55 PST. Median p95 for generation requests jumped from ~120ms to ~800ms and we’re also seeing a sustained ~4.8% 5xx rate on the production model routes (v2.3). This is affecting payment authorization flows for a subset of customers — about 12% of total volume.

We rely on Redwood for predictable latency; this is causing timeouts in our transaction pipeline. Can you confirm if there are ongoing deploys, region issues, or throttling? We're pausing large batches but throughput is still degraded. Attaching a short snapshot of our internal logs (attachment: ef_logs_snapshot.txt).

We need an urgent ETA and mitigation steps. If you have a private bridge, please spin it up — we can join immediately.

Thanks,

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Neha / team —

Quick technical snapshot from infra:
- No active deploys to v2.3 in the last 72h.
- us-west-2 GPU pool hitting transient queue growth at ~08:00 PST due to increased traffic from a retail batch (not EdgeFin). Kernel hot-paths for KV cache misses spiked; we saw memory pressure on a small subset of instances (3/120 nodes) which created local retries and downstream 5xx.
- Autoscaler attempted to add capacity but there was a 7m lag due to a recent image prefetch throttling on the subnet.

Mitigation steps executed at 08:40 PST:
1) Evicted the three affected pods and restarted on fresh nodes (repartitioned KV cache).
2) Temporary routing policy: route EdgeFin traffic to reserved standby nodes (dedicated pool) for the next 2 hours to avoid noisy neighbors.
3) Increased retry-backoff on proxy to lower amplified load.

Observed outcome: p95 reduced from ~800ms -> ~240ms by 09:00 PST; 5xx fell from 4.8% -> 0.6%. Still above normal; monitoring for residuals.

Next actions (ETA):
- 09:30 PST: Full cache warm-up and telemetry check across all regions. If stable, we'll keep standby routing for 3 hours then progressively shift back.
- 10:15 PST: Incident summary and customer-facing note drafted for Neha to send.

I am attaching a small diagnostic snapshot: edgefin_incident_snapshot_20261215.json (contains pod-level metrics, anonymized traces).

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Samir —

Thank you for the quick heads-up and patience. Short executive summary and immediate actions we took:

What happened (summary):
- Around 07:55 PST an unrelated high-throughput batch job caused transient queueing on a subset of us-west-2 inference nodes. That led to KV cache miss amplification and local memory pressure on 3 nodes which created retries and a spike in 5xxs and p95 latency for v2.3 routes.

Actions we executed (08:40 — 09:00 PST):
- Evicted and reprovisioned the 3 affected pods on fresh nodes.
- Temporarily routed EdgeFin production traffic to a reserved standby pool to isolate you from noisy neighbors.
- Tuned proxy retry/backoff to avoid load amplification.

Immediate impact:
- p95 improved from ~800ms -> ~240ms; 5xx fell from 4.8% -> 0.6%.
- Customer-facing authorization flows returned to steady state for the majority of traffic; we observed a small cohort (~1.2% of requests) still experiencing elevated tail latency during warm-up windows.

Next steps and timeline:
- 10:30 PST: Complete KV cache warm-up; monitor for residual tail spikes.
- 11:00 PST: Start progressive traffic shift from standby pool back to standard routing over 30 minutes if telemetry remains stable.
- 12:00 PST: Deliver a formal incident report including root cause analysis and recommended hardening (auto-scaler tweaks and prefetch concurrency improvements). Attached is a draft incident summary (incident_summary_v1.pdf) and the diagnostic snapshot Jonas shared.

Compensation / SLA:
- We will submit this for a standard SLA review and are prepared to propose a credit if the rolling window shows customer impact beyond thresholds. I'll coordinate with your procurement team if needed.

Bridge details: Zoom link https://zoom.company/bridge/edgefin-1215 (we're on the call 24/7 until resolved).

Please let me know if you'd like Redwood execs on a quick 15-minute sync — Laura is on cc and can join.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
